A quick brief on the OLED market and current overstocked inventory issues…
Santa Clara, California-based Coherent Inc. (COHR) manufactures many types of lasers including lasers used for OLED backplane crystallization (Excimer Laser Annealing) and for FRIT welding (also referred to as glass soldering or seal glass bonding) of OLED displays.
The largest and only manufacturer at scale, able to deliver to the high-demand growth markets for OLED screens (used for instance, in the latest Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) iPhone products, Samsung (OTC:SSNLF) Galaxy S9, and multiple displays which bear the OLED technology), is Samsung
Recent reports have indicated a slowdown (albeit temporary in my opinion) for products like the iPhone X, which has directly impacted the inventory for OLED products within Samsung’s warehouses. This build-up of inventory has led to Samsung’s decision to halt production, without dropping the price/margins (due to the high production costs for OLED) and allow inventory to reduce organically before production can resume.
Current fundamentals in favour of COHR (most recent quarter) include
Sales Growth of 13.78% Operating Margin Growth of 2.07% EBIT/EV Yield of 11.32% Free-Cash-Flow/EV Yield of 7.66% Low Debt to Equity Ratio of 35%
(Source: WSJ)
From Samsung’s perspective, the halting of production, combined with organic reduction of inventory at non-discounted prices indicates confidence in the demand for OLED in the near-to-medium term future, to remain robust, rendering the overstock a temporary situation.
The important take from this is that Samsung has few if any competitors who are able to deliver at the high production scale they are capable of. And part of the supply chain for OLED, which essentially include COHR, which rely on Samsung’s order book, are also suffering from the halt in OLED production, albeit temporary.
Keep in mind that OLED is not the only product within Coherent’s range. In fact, OLED is a sub-division of the microelectronics segment (which contributed to just over half of total Q2 revenue). Put into perspective, while OLED represents an important proportion of sales, possibly accounting for majority part of the microelectronics segment, it is not the only game in town for COHR. Additional products from a diversified portfolio include fiber lasers, OEM components and instrumentation, medical OEMs, and products which currently serve wider growth market opportunities in defense and aerospace.
To this effect, the company announced: “We experienced a surge in demand across a number of end markets during our second fiscal quarter. Orders for high power fiber lasers were up significantly from metal cutting OEMs in China, Tier 1 automotive component suppliers and EV battery manufacturers. Semiconductor capital equipment orders benefitted from high fab utilization rates and Chinese IC investments as part of Made in China 2025. Bookings across the OEM component and instrumentation space were up due to annual buys in bioinstrumentation, strength from medical OEMs and increasing opportunities in defense and aerospace.” (Source: PME Newswire).
The reason for the stock price becoming oversold is investors’ [rightful] perception and determination that OLED is a very integral component of the ‘growth’ story for COHR going into the future. In other words, while COHR is diversified to a general extent, with various product lines, as indicated above, the markets for these products (with the possible exception of electric vehicle (EV) battery welding, which I will go into in a moment) can only be expected to have gradual/conservative expectations of sales revenue growth, purely based on those products not being within high-demand growth sectors like OLED (and potentially large-scale EV battery welding).
(Source: Finviz)
It is worth pointing out as an extension to the fact that OLED inventory is ‘temporarily’ overstocked, there remains a likelihood – just one [well-regarded] analyst pointing out that OLED excess inventory is reducing, preferably supported by Samsung announcing a resumption of OLED production (which will happen in time), and COHR will be at the forefront of investor’s minds – provided a strong basis for a rally in the stock price.
Another important growth market which should not be underestimated is the chain of production involved in electric vehicle batteries. This is certainly a growth market which COHR can (and likely will) benefit from in the longer term, owning the technology and solution, together with competitor IPG Photonics (IPGP) for welding Lithium-Ion batteries. Supporting this, here’s what Northcoast Research analyst Tom Hayes had to say about the growth in Lithium Batteries and his mention on how this will directly impact companies like IPG Photonics and COHR…
The analyst stated: “the primary drivers for battery demand will come from electric vehicles, electrical storage from non-traditional electrical generation sources (solar, wind), consumer electronics (mobile/smartphones, personal computers), and industrial tools. According to Loup Ventures, sales of hybrid and electric vehicles should grow from around 2.5 million units in 2016 to around 22 million units in 2025. The global market for Li-ion batteries in light duty and medium/heavy duty vehicles is expected to grow from $7.8 billion in 2015 to $30.6 billion in 2024 and actual demand could be significantly higher as the Chinese government has instituted extremely favorable incentives for adoption of EV’s…”
Hayes further noted, “IPG Photonics and Coherent both have solutions which can address the welding of batteries.” (Source: StreetInsider)
This is a potentially significant growth market for COHR, which forms part of its inherently diversified product lines. Moreover, it demonstrates how pure focus on the temporary situation that is the OLED screens, does not warrant the currently oversold stock price in COHR – which in my view will not remain at the currently low levels for long. At the current price of $168.59, COHR trades at an EBITDA/EV multiple of 8.11 (Source: Gurufocus), representing a historically low valuation, with – in my opinion – limited downside and a stronger case for a rally in the short-to-medium term, as Samsung maintains a handle on resolving the short OLED oversupply issues.
Disclosure: I/we have no positions in any stocks mentioned, but may initiate a long position in COHR over the next 72 hours.
